title: Release window slot marketplace — design & runbook for OKR-aligned capacity allocation
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: As release volume and cross-surface (runtime/console/API) feature launches increase, product teams fight for the same limited launch windows and reserved Dedicated capacity. Current ad-hoc booking (calendar email and slack channels) causes missed coordination, last-minute throttles, and uneven OKR prioritization.

Proposed solution: Build a 'Release Window Slot Marketplace' in the Redwood Console — a lightweight allocation service + UI where teams request, bid, and reserve launch slots backed by capacity credits and risk budgets. The marketplace enforces OKR priority weighting, autoscaling credit limits, and region SLO guardrails to surface safe, prioritized scheduling across hosted, dedicated, and private surfaces.

Scope (MVP):
- Console UX: slot request form (target surface, capacity estimate, expected peak qps, region, OKR tag, blackout windows, canary window preference) + calendar view showing available/claimed slots and regional capacity hedges.
- Backend: slot registry service with TTL, capacity-credit accounting, conflict resolution policy, and soft-reservation tokens.
- Policy: OKR-weighted priority algorithm, risk budget consumption tracking, and automatic fallback lanes (e.g., smaller model variant / reduced batch size) assigned at allocation-time.
- Integrations: link allocations to rollout runbooks, create automated GitHub PR check that references slot ID for release pipelines, and expose slot telemetry to Console launch dashboard.

Out of scope for MVP: deep financial marketplace (no tokenized trading), complex auction mechanics, or SSO-level billing changes.

Why this matters: Reduces cross-team friction, ties launch priority to measurable OKR objectives, and surfaces capacity constraints earlier so infra can pre-warm Dedicated pools or recommend mitigations (quantized model variants, regional shifts).
acceptance_criteria: Console: teams can create a slot request with required fields and see provisional / confirmed status in calendar UI
Backend: slot registry enforces TTL and prevents double-booking for the same region/capacity pool
Policy: OKR tag influences slot ordering and is surfaced to approvers in the UI
Integration: creating a slot produces a slot-id that can be referenced in a GitHub PR (sample PR check shown)
Observability: launch dashboard shows slot consumption, credit usage, and a small-sample preflight simulation (5 requests) showing predicted latency impact
success_metrics: Reduction in last-minute slot conflicts by 70% in first 6 weeks
>80% of launch slots created with OKR tag filled with required approvals
Average time-to-resolve slot conflict decreases from 48h to <6h
Number of launches that required emergency capacity hedges down 50%
stakeholders: Ravi Menon (Infra Eng) — backend allocation service
runbook_steps: Step 0 — Discovery: interview top 8 teams to map weekly launch demand (done, notes in Confluence)
Step 1 — Prototype: Console mock + slot API contract (link below) for internal alpha
Step 2 — Alpha: enable slot marketplace for 2 pilot teams (runtime team + Console infra), collect telemetry for 2 sprints
Step 3 — Policy tuning: adjust OKR weighting and TTL based on alpha data
Step 4 — Beta: open to 25% of org; integrate GitHub PR check and rollout pipeline validation
Step 5 — GA: enable cross-surface auto-suggestion (runtime/console/api) and reserved capacity pre-warm triggers
notes: Discovery summary: weekly peak launch demand concentrated on Tue/Thu mornings (PST) — consider soft blackout hedges on those lanes
Design decision (2025-02-20): use soft-reservation tokens with a 72h TTL before confirmed allocation; hard confirmations require a capacity-credit spend
Trade-off: soft reservations lower admin friction but can reduce predictability for Dedicated pre-warm — will add capacity-hedge override for high-priority OKRs
Regulatory note: private/on-prem customers cannot be auto-allocated to shared Dedicated pools — slot flow will surface 'private-only' flag and routing policy
